subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for October 23, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

articles.title: Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
articles.summary: Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset.

articles.title: Cluster Versus Individual Randomization in Prehospital, Emergency and Critical Care Trials: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.summary: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes. Using absolute ln(odds ratio [OR]) for mortality and absolute Hedges' g for the secondary outcome, mean differences (MDs) in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs were analyzed using mixed regression models, presented with 95% CIs. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT). We included 65 meta-analyses in quantitative analyses, encompassing 212 randomized clinical trials (39 cRCTs and 173 iRCTs) and 315,276 patients.
